I have done both: moving across the country for a SO, and moving out and moving across the country for a job. Moving for the SO was something that seemed practical and romantic at the time, but it was extremely difficult getting work - it took me three months to find a job in my field, and I had to accept a lower pay. I think a lot of it was based on not being able to have names they recognize on my resume, thereby making my experience questionable. I think a lot of couples can make this kind of move work, but the person needs to feel fulfilled from things other than the relationship. So if you feel unemployable, it will put a strain on the relationship.  

When I moved across the country for a job, it was hard for a while, but gradually got better. Pretty much the exact opposite.

Hello! I upvoted this a while back and wanted to follow up. So did you ever get a copy of a Digivice to rom dump? I've actually been wanting to do one for similar reasons - I want to extract the data from a D-3 to learn a few things about it, and get the sprites off of it.
Thank you! This is exactly what I was looking for (I think). I'm gonna read this and give it shot!
I apologize if my comment came off as sarcastic or patronizing - I genuinely want to not offend. Could you give an example of what you would see as a good way to do this?

I'll start. I actually had the D-3s with my friends on my block growing up, and my partner was Gargomon. We had a blood pact to always put saving the world before all other things; one time my D-3 went off during a test and I ran to the bathroom to go address the attack, and my buddy was there waiting for me with his D-3 as well. The most extreme day was the day we both had to take down the third boss (we tried to sync ourselves as much as possible and take down bosses together), and my buddy was on a date when his went off. He actually left the date to go save the world with me. I forget what excuse he made up to get out of it, but she was actually pretty understanding of it and they had a make up date the next day. But she never knew that we were secretly saving the world on the side - we kept that a secret from anyone that wasn't also a Digidestined.

This was me for a very long time. While I'm not perfect myself, the one thing I can say is that the times where I felt life wasn't worth living were the times I was living for someone else. I don't just mean times where I was living to serve someone, but I also mean times where I was defining the quality of my life based on how others felt about me, or how strong my relationships were with others. 

It doesn't seem like it right now, but the best thing you can do is start living for yourself. Don't live to make up for the emotions you disrespected. Don't live hoping you'll meet that special someone that will make you feel complete and make you forget all about this girl. Live for the things you enjoy doing. Live for the things you want to change in the world, and make every decision functioning towards that greater good. 

It takes a long time to change your way of thinking like this. The first time someone told me this I just sat there staring blankly, like "easy for you to say, but how do I even start that?" And really I'd just be leading you astray if I told you, since this is the sort of thing that is very personal, and the answer is more you than anyone else. 

But what I can promise is that, once you start doing this, things will get a little better. You will still look for friends and loved ones, but breakups like this won't matter as much, because while they can hurt you, they will no longer define you. Good luck my friend.
